name: Sun
notes: Our familiar G2V star — calibration anchor for habitability.

name: Alpha Centauri A
notes: Closest G-type star to Earth; binary with Alpha Cen B.

name: Tau Ceti
notes: Old, quiet G-type star with multiple known planets.

name: 51 Pegasi
notes: First sun-like star found to host an exoplanet (1995).

name: Alpha Centauri B
notes: K-dwarf companion to Alpha Cen A; quiet, mature.

name: Epsilon Eridani
notes: Young K-dwarf with mild flare activity and a debris disk.

name: Sigma Draconis
notes: Quiet K-dwarf about 19 light-years away.

name: Proxima Centauri
notes: Closest star to the Sun; flare-active red dwarf hosting Proxima b.

name: Barnard's Star
notes: Very old, mostly quiet M-dwarf; second-closest stellar system.

name: TRAPPIST-1
notes: Ultracool M-dwarf with seven known terrestrial planets, three in HZ.

name: Teegarden's Star
notes: Old, quiet ultracool M-dwarf.

name: Gliese 581
notes: Quiet M3V; multi-planet system, a couple of HZ candidates.

name: LHS 1140
notes: Quiet, old M-dwarf hosting LHS 1140 b — a promising rocky HZ planet.

name: Procyon A
notes: F-type subgiant; brightest F star in our sky.

name: Beta Comae Berenices
notes: Sun-like F-dwarf, often used as a Solar analogue.

name: Sirius A
notes: Brightest star in Earth's night sky; hot A-type main-sequence star.

name: Vega
notes: Has a debris disk; possible planets.

name: Altair
notes: Rapidly rotating A-type star, oblate from spin.

name: Rigel
notes: Blue supergiant; intense UV; planets implausible.

name: Zeta Puppis
notes: Massive O-type supergiant; UV-dominated; planets unlikely.
